p.docTitle:
Ordinance
on the Use of «Switzerland»
or «Swiss» for Watches

preamble.p:
on the basis of Article 50 paragraph 2 of the Trade Mark Protection Act of
28 August 1992
SR 232.11 (TmPA),
Amended by No I of the O of 17 June 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 2593).

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 17 June 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 2593).

item.p: time-measuring devices intended to be worn on the wrist;

blockList.listIntroduction: devices whose main function is to measure time and whose movement:

item.p: does not exceed 60 mm in width, length or diameter, or
does not exceed 14 mm in thickness measured with the plate and bridges.

content.p: When determining the width, length, diameter and thickness, only the technically necessary dimensions are taken into consideration.
The component that enables the watch to be worn is not included in the definition of the term «watch» specified in paragraph 1.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 27 May 1992 (AS 1992 1229). Amended by No I of the O of 17 June 2016, with the exception of let. a, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2016 2593). See also the transitional provision of this amendment at the end of the text.

blockList.listIntroduction: A watch is considered to be a Swiss watch if:
at least the following elements of its technical development are carried out in Switzerland:

item.p: for exclusively mechanical watches: the mechanical construction and prototyping of the watch as a whole,
for watches that are not exclusively mechanical: the mechanical construction and prototyping of the watch as a whole, as well as the design of the printed circuits, the display and the software;
its movement is Swiss;
its movement is cased up in Switzerland;
the final inspection of the watch is conducted by the manufacturer in Switzerland; and
at least 60 per cent of the manufacturing costs are incurred in Switzerland.

article.heading:
Definition of a Swiss movement
Amended by No I of the O of 17 June 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 2593).

blockList.listIntroduction:
A movement is considered to be a Swiss movement if:

item.p: for exclusively mechanical watch movements: the mechanical construction and prototyping of the watch movement as a whole,

for watch movements that are not exclusively mechanical: the mechanical construction and prototyping of the watch as a whole, as well as the design of the printed circuits, the display and the software;

item.num:

item.p:
the constituent parts made in Switzerland, excluding the cost of assembling them, represent at least 50 per cent of the value of all of the constituent parts.
Amended by No I of the O of 27 May 1992, in force since 1 July 1992 (AS 1992 1229).

blockList.listIntroduction: To calculate the value of the constituent parts made in Switzerland in accordance with paragraph 1 letter c, the following rules apply:

item.num:
a.
Repealed by No I of the O of 17 June 2016, with effect from 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 2593).

abis.
Inserted by No I of the O of 17 June 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 2593).

blockList.listIntroduction: the cost of the dial is included if the dial:

item.p: performs an electronic function for the watch, and
is used to equip the watch with an electro-optical display or a solar module;

assembly costs may be taken into consideration if a certification procedure provided for in an international treaty ensures that, as a result of close industrial cooperation, foreign and Swiss constituent parts are equivalent in quality;

item.num:
c.
Inserted by No I of the O of 17 June 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 2593).
item.p: the assembly costs taken into consideration may not exceed the value of the foreign constituent parts recognised as being equivalent that are incorporated into the Swiss movement concerned.

content.p:
The provisions of the Additional Agreement of 20 July 1972
SR 0.632.290.131 to the Agreement concerning products of the clock and watch industry between the European Economic Community and its Member States and the Swiss Confederation applies.
Inserted by No I of the O of 17 June 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 2593).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 17 June 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 2593).

blockList.listIntroduction: Constituent parts are considered to be Swiss if:

item.p: they are inspected by the manufacturer in Switzerland; and
at least 60 per cent of their manufacturing costs are incurred in Switzerland.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 17 June 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 2593).

blockList.listIntroduction: A watch movement is considered to have been assembled in Switzerland within the meaning of Article 2 paragraph 1 letter abis if all of the constituent parts are assembled in Switzerland. Only the subassembly of the following constituent parts may be carried out abroad:

item.p: for exclusively mechanical watch movements: the gear trains;

blockList.listIntroduction: for watch movements that are not exclusively mechanical:

item.p: the electronic modules,
the electro-optical display modules,
the energy collecting module,
the regulating organ,
the gear trains,
the motor or motors, including the rotors and coils they are made of.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 17 June 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 2593).

blockList.listIntroduction: Excluded from the calculation of the manufacturing costs are:

item.p: costs for natural products which, due to natural conditions, cannot be produced in Switzerland;
costs for materials which, for objective reasons, are not available in Switzerland in sufficient quantities, up to their unavailability rate;
packaging costs;
transport costs;
costs for the commercialisation of the goods, as well as costs for marketing and customer service;
the cost of the battery.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 17 June 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 2593).

article.heading: Materials unavailable in sufficient quantities in Switzerland

content.p:
If the watchmaking industry publishes information in accordance with Article 52k of the Trade Mark Protection Ordinance of 23 December 1992
SR 232.111 about materials that are not available in sufficient quantities in Switzerland, it shall ensure that such information is objectively justified. In the event of disagreement within the industry, it will consult with independent third parties.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 27 May 1992, in force since 1 July 1992 (AS 1992 1229). See also the final provision of this amendment at the end of the text.

article.heading:
Requirements for using «Switzerland» or «Swiss» and the Swiss cross
Amended by No I of the O of 17 June 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 2593).

blockList.listIntroduction: The following may be used exclusively for Swiss watches and Swiss watch movements:

item.p: the designation «Switzerland»;
designations such as «Swiss», «Swiss product», «Made in Switzerland», «Swiss quality» and other designations containing «Switzerland» or «Swiss» or designations that could be confused with them;

the Swiss cross and other signs that could be confused with it.
Amended by No I of the O of 17 June 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 2593).

content.p:
Swiss indications of source for specific activities in accordance with Article 47 paragraph 3ter TmPA
SR 232.11 are only permitted if the indication is not understood by the relevant public as an indication of source for the product as a whole.
Inserted by No I of the O of 17 June 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 2593).
If the watch is not Swiss, the designations specified in paragraph 1 may still be placed on Swiss movements, provided that they are not visible to the buyer.

The indication «Swiss movement» may be placed on watches that contain a Swiss movement. The word «movement» must be written in full and must be of the same typeface, size and colour as the designation «Swiss».

Paragraphs 1 and 3 also apply when these designations are used either in translation or with the indication of the actual origin of the watch, or with the addition of words such as «kind», «type», «style» or other combinations of words.

blockList.listIntroduction: In addition to the placing of these designations on the watch or its packaging, the following constitute use:

item.p: the sale, the offering for sale or the placing on the market of watches bearing such a designation;
the placing of these designations on shop signs, advertisements, prospectuses, invoices, business letters or business papers.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 18 Oct. 1978, in force since 1 Jan. 1979 (AS 1978 1620).

article.heading:
Placing the designation of origin
a. on watch cases

blockList.listIntroduction: A watch case is considered to be Swiss if:

item.p: at least one essential manufacturing process is carried out in Switzerland (i.e. stamping, machining or polishing);
it is assembled in Switzerland;
it is inspected in Switzerland by the manufacturer; and

at least 60 per cent of the manufacturing costs are incurred in Switzerland.
Amended by No I of the O of 17 June 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2017 (AS 2016 2593).

content.p:
The designations specified in Article 3 paragraphs 1 and 4 may only be placed on watch cases intended for watches within the meaning of Article 1a.
Amended by No I of the O of 29 March 1995, in force since 1 May 1995 (AS 1995 1218).

The indication «Swiss case» or a translation thereof may be placed on Swiss cases intended to be fitted to watches that are not Swiss watches within the meaning of Article 1a. Where such indications are placed on the exterior of the case, the origin of the watch or the watch movement must be visibly indicated on the watch.
Amended by No I of the O of 29 March 1995, in force since 1 May 1995 (AS 1995 1218).

…
Repealed by No I of the O of 29 March 1995, with effect from 1 May 1995(AS 1995 1218).

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 27 May 1992, in force since 1 July 1992 (AS 1992 1229).

content.p:
The designations specified in Article 3 paragraphs 1 and 4 may only be placed on dials intended for watches within the meaning of Article 1a. …
Second sentence repealed by No I of the O of 29 Mar. 1995, with effect from 1 May 1995 (AS 1995 1218).
The indication «Swiss dial» or a translation thereof may be placed on the back of Swiss dials intended for watches that are not Swiss within the meaning of Article 1a.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 18 Oct. 1978 (AS 1978 1620). Amended by No I of the O of 29 March 1995, in force since 1 May 1995 (AS 1995 1218).

article.heading: c. on other constituent parts of the watch

content.p: The designations specified in Article 3 paragraphs 1 and 4 may only be placed on constituent parts intended for watches within the meaning of Article 1a.
Swiss movement-blanks that are exported and watch movements manufactured using such blanks may bear the indication «Swiss parts».

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 18 Oct. 1978, in force since 1 Jan. 1979 (AS 1978 1620).

blockList.listIntroduction:
Notwithstanding Article 3 paragraph 2 and Articles 4 to 6, watch cases, dials, watch movements and other constituent parts may bear Swiss designations of origin if they are:
Amended by No I of the O of 27 May 1992, in force since 1 July 1992 (AS 1992 1229).

item.p: exported individually as samples or collections of samples;
manufactured in Switzerland and
not intended for sale.

authorialNote.p: Originally Art. 6. Amended by No I of the O of 23 Dec. 1992, in force since 1 April 1993 (AS 1993 312).

content.p: Any breach of this Ordinance is subject to the criminal provisions of the TmPA.
This Ordinance comes into force on 1 January 1972.

proviso.heading:
Final Provision of the Amendment of 27 May 1992
AS 1992 1229

content.p: Undertakings that have already lawfully and consistently used one of the designations protected under Article 3 paragraphs 1 and 4 prior to this amendment coming into force are authorised to continue to use this designation for five years after this amendment has come into force, even if the casing up and final inspection are carried out by the manufacturer abroad.

transitional.heading:
Transitional Provisions to the Amendment of 17 June 2016
AS 2016 2593

content.p: 1 Watches and watch movements manufactured between 1 January 2017 and 31 December 2018 that do not fulfil the conditions specified in Article 1a letter a and Article 2 paragraph 1 letter a may be placed on the market for the first time with an indication of source that complies with the law in force at the time of manufacture only until 31 December 2020.

blockList.listIntroduction: 2 The calculation of the manufacturing costs of a watch may exclude the costs of watch cases and watch glass that:

item.p: a manufacturer already had in stock prior to 31 December 2016; and
were incorporated into a watch prior to 31 December 2018.
